newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly lower, except silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly lower, except silver.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, on moderate volumes, with the exception of silver.

"Gold and silver look to be very slowly making longer term bottoming moves, but I think I could grow old and be retired before anything significant happens," said Hans Kashyap, president of Analytics Research Corp in Maryland.
COMEX August gold ended down $1.10 at $343.70 an ounce, with the weak downtrend since early May still seen intact, though support has held three times around $343.00 an ounce, analysts noted.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.50/00, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $342.15 and the New York close Monday around $342.40/90.
Meanwhile, COMEX July silver ended up 7.5 cents at $4.762 an ounce, on estimated COMEX silver volume of 24,000 lots.
July silver has been in a $4.65-4.90 range since mid-May, with good industrial demand seen below $4.70 and ample supply seen near $4.90, analysts said.
COMEX silver stocks fell a further 3,500,592 ounces to 190,990,070 ounces in data released late Monday, as the build to over 200 million ounces in May reversed.

Silver is still seen having slightly better fundamentals than gold, without the overhang of potential central bank sales to cap the market, as silver enters the ninth year of a shortfall between world silver mine production and fabrication demand.
"Silver is starting to look interesting, with a long basing action in progress, and could wind up being the next strong metals market," Kashyap said.

Meanwhile, NYMEX July platinum lost a further $12.80 to close at $411.10 an ounce, and has now given back about half of its gains since mid-April, after running up to a contract high at $473.80 on June 6.

As funds continued to liquidate long positions ahead of July platinum's delivery period, open interest in July platinum fell a further 1,247 lots Monday to 10,445 contracts, while open interest in the October and January contracts rose.
July platinum sees its first notice day in two weeks time, with open interest equivalent to 522,250 ounces still outstanding against NYMEX platinum stocks of 54,700 ounces.
In the physical market, spot platinum saw a seven-year high at $500 in early June, but has now given back about 60 percent of its gains since the start of the year.
NYMEX September palladium ended down $2.90 at $177.90, after seeing a contract high last Friday at $192.00.

Spot palladium has only given back about 30 percent of its gains since late 1996, after doubling in price and seeing a 17 year high this month, under the impact of an acute shortage of metal due to a five month suspension of Russian exports.
In overnight news, Norilsk Nickel first deputy chief executive Yuri Kotlyar was quoted by Russia's Itar-Tass news agency saying Russian exports of PGMs would resume late June.
But in the meantime the PGM market remained sharply backwardated and lease rates in the physical market remained high, traders said.
One month palladium lease rates remained over 100 percent Tuesday, with 12 month rates around 60 percent, PGM dealers said.
One month platinum lease rates were around 50 percent with 12 month rates around 25 percent.
"We're not too worried about the return of the Russians to the PGM market," Kashyap said.
"From a technical point of view, we've seen unbelievable fireworks and PGMs still look good, with the recent downward reactions still contained within the uptrends," he said.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
